title: Non-profit child care growth and outreach funding accountability
subtitle: Committee deferred a motion on A Better Tent City metrics; Schwaben Club lease and fee-for-service review discussed.
overview: The Community and Health Services Committee recommended that Regional staff explore creating community-based non-profit child care spaces on Regionally owned land and buildings, surplus lands and Waterloo Region Housing redevelopments {{vote:m2}}. Staff also would consult area municipalities, school boards, post-secondary institutions, hospitals and businesses. Staff said non-profit spaces are currently about 60% of the total against a target of 85%, and the waitlist for licensed child care has grown to 9,200 children.

A notice of motion would have directed staff to collect outcomes, data and metrics from A Better Tent City, which received a Council-approved grant in the 2024 budget. Questions arose about procedure and about whether the organization had been told the item was on the agenda. The committee deferred the motion to February 21, 2024 {{vote:m4}}.

The committee also received an infection prevention inspection report on the consent agenda. Staff said they will report in April on the Schwaben Club shelter lease, which ends this summer, including community engagement with neighbours and area municipalities. The committee then went into closed session.

decisions.item: Non-profit child care spaces on Regional land
decisions.detail: The committee recommended that staff explore community-based non-profit child care spaces on Regionally owned land and buildings, surplus lands, Waterloo Region Housing redevelopments and other opportunities.

decisions.item: Partner consultation on child care space
decisions.detail: The committee recommended that Children's Services, Housing Services and Economic Development staff consult area municipalities, school boards, universities, colleges, hospitals and businesses about affordable non-profit child care in under-utilized buildings and land.

decisions.item: Deferral of A Better Tent City metrics motion
decisions.detail: The committee deferred the amended notice of motion on collecting outcomes and metrics from A Better Tent City to February 21, 2024.
The committee received the 2023 Infection Prevention and Control Inspection Program Report for information and approved the consent agenda.

debate: Supporters of the metrics motion said any organization receiving Regional funding should provide comparable outcome data. They said it would also inform any future request to extend the grant, and some asked for a general accountability policy for funded groups.

A councillor raised a point of order that the motion amounted to reconsidering a decision already confirmed by by-law. The clerks advised it concerned metrics and not the funding itself, and the chair accepted that view. The sponsor then removed the wording "prior to the distribution of funding".

Another councillor said the organization should have been told the item was on the agenda so it could delegate. Staff said they do not normally contact community partners about items not yet debated, and this concern led to the deferral.

Staff said data collected from other outreach providers includes referrals, unique households served, service restrictions and a year-end narrative. Some councillors said the real question was why the group did not meet the original funding criteria.

On child care, councillors asked why growth is prioritized for non-profits. Staff said the federal program directs growth to the non-profit sector, which is considered better able to provide sustainable, high-quality care, and that existing for-profit operators can still take part.
